test_cases.title: GET /api/v1/student/{studentId} returns 200 with full student body when the id exists
test_cases.given: a student with id 1 (name, email, dob) exists in the student table
test_cases.then: the response is 200 OK with a JSON body containing id=1, name, email, dob, and a computed age field, matching the shape of a row from the existing GET /api/v1/student list endpoint

test_cases.title: GET /api/v1/student/{studentId} returns 404 (not 500) when the id does not exist
test_cases.given: no student with id 999 exists in the student table
test_cases.then: the response is 404 Not Found with a JSON error body; the response is NOT a generic 500 from an uncaught IllegalStateException

test_cases.title: GET /api/v1/student/{studentId} with a negative or zero id returns 404, not an error
test_cases.given: no student exists with a negative id (-1) or id 0
test_cases.when: a client calls GET /api/v1/student/-1 and GET /api/v1/student/0
test_cases.then: both requests return 404 Not Found (the negative/zero value is numeric so Long conversion succeeds; the not-found path applies, not a 400)

test_cases.title: 404 response body for a missing student contains no stack trace or internal exception identifier
test_cases.given: no student with id 999 exists in the student table
test_cases.then: the 404 response body contains no stack trace, exception class name, or internal identifier — only Spring's default error JSON fields (status, error, message, timestamp, path)

last_run.note: Response body is fully empty (Content-Length: 0), not Spring's default {status,error,message,timestamp,path} JSON shape — ResponseEntity.notFound().build() bypasses BasicErrorController entirely. This is a stricter negative (zero fields of any kind, so trivially no forbidden fields) than the then-clause's literal phrasing anticipated; treated as PASS on the whitelist reading. README.md:589 documents this exact empty-body behavior as intended.
